advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize line endings (CRLF/CR -> LF) before computing review_bounded_description_chars so AC-char crediting matches raw len(description).
evidence:
material_diff.py:85 normalizes before processing: `text = description.replace("
", "
").replace("", "
")` — evaluate_plan_clarity/review_bounded_description_chars do NOT
splitlines() also splits on Unicode line boundaries (\u2028, \x0c, \x85, etc.) which len(line)+1 mis-accounts against raw len()
advisory.finding: review_bounded_description_chars charges AC chars as sum(len(line)+1) per splitlines() line while subtracting from raw len(description); on CRLF (\r\n) descriptions the line terminator is 2 chars but only 1 is credited back per AC line, so AC items are under-credited and review-bounded prose is over-charged. Unlike the rest of the plan-review pipeline, this path does not normalize line endings first.
scenarios: A near-cap CRLF-terminated ticket description with a multi-line AC section is over-charged and can be blocked (or the AC-correction deadlock re-appears) even though the LF-normalized content is within cap

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Base the trailing-newline (-1) adjustment on whether the last AC item is actually the document's final line, not on whether the whole text ends with a newline.
evidence: src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py:188-189: `if acc.ac_item_chars and not text_ends_with_newline:` / `acc.ac_item_chars[-1] = max(acc.ac_item_chars[-1] - 1, 0)`
The condition keys off `text.endswith(("\n","\r"))` (line 153) for the whole document, not off whether the last AC item is the final line

test_p4_charges_prose_after_acceptance_criteria_section (tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py:135) constructs exactly this shape (AC item then '## Later' + non-newline-terminated prose), so the misattribution is reachable
advisory.finding: The trailing-newline correction subtracts 1 from ac_item_chars[-1] whenever the whole text lacks a trailing newline, but the last AC item may not be the document's last line (e.g. a '## Testing' or '## Later' section follows the AC block). In that case the last AC item's final line WAS followed by a newline in the source, so the -1 under-counts AC chars and over-charges review-bounded prose by 1.
scenarios: A ticket whose AC section is followed by a trailing '## Testing'/'## Later' section that does not end in a newline
advisory.suggested_fix: Track whether the final emitted line belonged to the last AC item and apply the -1 only then, or avoid the +1-per-line reconstruction by charging AC spans against the original text offsets.
